title: Reach Revenue Target
real_world_story: An advertising platform ranks advertisements by expected revenue and wants to know the minimum number of highest-revenue advertisements required to reach a target revenue.

real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Finding the smallest number of top advertisements needed to reach the target

problem_statement: Given N advertisement revenues and a target revenue R, sort the revenues in descending order and determine the minimum number of highest-revenue advertisements whose combined revenue is at least R. If the target cannot be reached using all advertisements, return -1.
task: Find the minimum number of top-revenue advertisements required to reach the target revenue.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N integers representing advertisement revenues. The third line contains an integer R representing the target revenue.
output_format: Print the minimum number of advertisements required to reach at least R. Print -1 if the total revenue of all advertisements is less than R.

examples.explanation: After sorting, the revenues are 1500, 1200, 900, 700, 400, 300. The first two advertisements generate 2700, reaching the target of 2500.
The sorted revenues are 700, 600, 500, 400, 300. The first three total 1800, while the first four total 2200, so four advertisements are required.

expected_algorithm.name: Binary Search
expected_algorithm.reason: After sorting the revenues and creating prefix sums, the prefix sums are non-decreasing. Binary search can find the smallest number of advertisements whose cumulative revenue reaches the target.

hint: Sort advertisement revenues in descending order.
Create a prefix sum of the sorted revenues.
Use binary search to find the first prefix sum that is at least R.
If no prefix sum reaches R, return -1.
real_world_takeaway: Binary search on cumulative revenue can quickly determine how many high-value advertisements are needed to meet a revenue target.
